review_type: Targeted closure of the original independent review

findings.title: Funding, schema and risk invariants on restart
findings.implementation: Engine.restore validates schema 2 and immutable identities, then reconstructs the state by replay and requires canonical equality. paper._load also validates both hashes, exact envelope version, finite nonboolean ordered timestamps, completion/execution-clock bounds and fault/control-history reconciliation.
findings.verified_evidence: Correctly rehashed envelopes containing cash=101, negative risk counters, a string pending flag, altered cached history or boolean schema version are rejected without rewriting the invalid journal. Legitimate profit survives replay: a $20 buy, partial $25 exit, failed exit and final $15 exit with $0.10 gas per attempt restore $119.60 cash and $19.60 closed-trade net P&L. Eight malformed or unordered outer timestamp variants are rejected.

findings.title: Observed UTC clock for paper risk and daily reporting
findings.implementation: Engine.step uses observed_at as paper execution/risk time and retains bar_ts separately. The post-fill risk update uses the same clock, Risk rejects backward clocks, and metrics assigns paper daily returns by observed_at.
findings.verified_evidence: Two attempted actions observed on the same UTC day cannot evade a $0.15 daily fee cap through the candle-start date: the first $0.10-gas fill executes, the second is rejected by daily_fee_cap. The fill timestamp is 86401, source bar timestamp is 86340, daily_return_count is 1, and a duplicate observation leaves the engine state hash unchanged. The repository additionally verifies the one-fill-per-day case.

findings.title: Failed-exit gas in closed-trade outcomes
findings.implementation: A failed attempt while a trade is active reduces current_trade.net_pnl. The event retains its side and gas; portfolio gas and realized account P&L remain accounted for separately.
findings.verified_evidence: The original losing example now reports both account and closed-trade P&L of -$0.05 and win_rate=0. A partial-exit/failure/final-exit example also reconciles to $19.60 profit and $0.40 gas, including after replay.

findings.title: Interval-aware source freshness and execution age
findings.implementation: Source staleness uses interval plus bounded grace. A separate new-bar execution-age check produces execution_late without filling an old observed price.
findings.verified_evidence: The healthy four-hour feed remains NO_NEW_COMPLETED_BAR at time 14500 after a close at 14400. A newly seen bar observed 91 seconds after its close is halted by the separate 90-second execution grace, with zero fills.

findings.title: All-overlap revision checking
findings.implementation: paper_step compares every stored bar that overlaps the incoming feed and durably records source_revision before re-raising a revision error.
findings.verified_evidence: Changing an older overlapping bar's volume, keeping the latest cached bar unchanged and adding a new bar cannot produce a fill. A later corrected feed remains halted with source_revision.

findings.title: Explicit current valuation after a halt
findings.implementation: Paper responses separate valuation from the historical processed-ledger metrics. They supply valuation.as_of_close, observation time, age/staleness, executable_quote=false, and ending_equity_as_of_close/equity_scope for the historical metrics.
findings.verified_evidence: After a network halt with $80 cash and two units, a fresh close at $1 reports current valuation=$82 as of close 180. Historical ending equity remains $100 explicitly as of processed close 120. Fills remain one; the valuation neither fabricates a liquidation nor extends the processed trading performance curve.

findings.title: Code, interpreter and strategy restart identity
findings.implementation: The runtime fingerprint covers every runtime *.py file and Python sys.version. The strategy fingerprint covers its class identity/source, instance settings and fixed strategy parameters. Both are stored and checked on restore.
findings.verified_evidence: Changing Python's recorded runtime version or trend fast=12 to fast=2 rejects restart. Schema-1 state is rejected. Old journals are intentionally not migrated or silently re-fingerprinted.

findings.title: Sticky faults at the paper abstraction boundary
findings.implementation: Data validation/revision faults are journaled inside the locked paper operation. record_fault persists initial network failure before any usable bar. The first invalid-data transition preserves a valid caller-supplied observation time; only an invalid clock is replaced with a valid wall-clock stamp.
findings.verified_evidence: Both an initial network failure and an initial NaN bar survive the first subsequent valid observation with HALTED_REQUIRES_REVIEW and zero fills. The explicit clock sequence 61 then 62 now works without injecting the wall clock into the journal. Existing-journal NaN/revision persistence is also covered by the repository suite.

findings.title: State/report path separation
findings.implementation: The CLI rejects canonical and same-file collisions between configured input, config, journal and report paths before fetching or writing.
findings.verified_evidence: Identical paths, a symlink alias and a hardlink alias all fail before the mocked fetch is called; the original file content remains unchanged.

findings.title: Historical completion boundaries
findings.implementation: fetch_bars parses against min(observed_at, before) and records completed_as_of separately. The research CSV runner and run_backtest API reject incomplete/future input against the current time.
findings.verified_evidence: With one-minute rows at 0, 60 and 120, before=120 and observed_at=180 return only starts 0 and 60, with completed_as_of=120. Direct year-2100 historical input is rejected. The full suite also exercises the future-CSV reporting-script rejection.

findings.title: Historical versus prospective evidence classification
findings.implementation: run_backtest explicitly reports execution_class=HISTORICAL_SIMULATION and prospective_observation=false, even if the supplied config mode is paper. The paper observer uses a separate prospective execution class.
findings.verified_evidence: A historical call with a paper config retains the explicit historical classification and false prospective flag. These fields do not assert qualified L4 performance or sustained operation.

residuals_discovered_and_closed_during_t.original_observation: Correctly rehashed schema-2 envelopes accepted malformed or unordered started_at/observed_at values.
residuals_discovered_and_closed_during_t.fix_verified: Finite nonboolean time validation, ordering and processed-source/execution-clock bounds now reject all eight independent cases.

residuals_discovered_and_closed_during_t.original_observation: An initial NaN-bar error at explicit now=61 persisted the actual wall clock, making a subsequent now=62 call fail as backward time.
residuals_discovered_and_closed_during_t.fix_verified: The valid supplied first-fault clock is now retained; the next valid observation reports the sticky halt.

limits: This is closure of the listed code defects, not a new full audit or a certification of all possible inputs.
No new public-network, wallet, live DEX, custody, signing, paid-service or legal/access test was performed.
Market results and prospective observations rerun by the implementer were not independently replicated in this closure.
Checksums/replay establish internal consistency and version identity, not authenticity against a writer who controls the full command log, source data and program.
The source intentionally rejects old schema/runtime/strategy journals rather than auto-migrating them.
The bounded command/file limits and lack of a continuous-service deployment remain operational scope limits; this review establishes no 90-day/100-trade qualification.
A halt remains an operational trigger rather than a guaranteed financial loss cap. Live remains DISABLED.
